note: Measured failures to meet a required neutralization outcome. An entry is a DEFECT, not a waiver: the suite pins the recorded measurement, so a component that regresses further fails and a component that is fixed fails until its entry is deleted and the ceiling lowered. Nothing here is excused; everything here is owed. `publicBehaviourChange: true` marks the entries whose fix is breaking and therefore belongs to the release lane, not to a security packet.

deviations.reason: No URL policy exists anywhere in packages/core/src — no scheme check, no allowlist, no normalization — so the `href` prop is written to the anchor `href` with no inspection (DzButton.vue template, `:href="isAnchor && !resolvedDisabled ? …"`). A `javascript:` URL supplied by whatever populates this component's items therefore executes in the host's own origin when a person clicks the link. Not fixed here: refusing these schemes is a breaking change, because `javascript:void(0)` is a widespread legacy idiom that today renders and would then stop, so the fix belongs to the release lane (TASK-N5-02) alongside the ARIA-prop gaps rather than to a fixture packet.

The same absent policy, on the two schemes that cannot execute: `file:` cannot be navigated to from a web page and a foreign-origin `blob:` resolves to nothing. The residual harm is a link that looks operable and is not, and an allowlist that would admit a scheme with no business in a web document. Recorded separately from the executable schemes so that closing the high-severity half does not appear to close this half with it.
